w: In the morning assembly Lord Harikrishna Maharaj was honored by devotees.

National Family and Children's Shibir ( 25 to 27 June) At 6.10 pm Swamishri arrived at the University of Nottingham campus, Nottingham, for a three - day National Family Shibir (camp)and Children's Shibir.

A total of 1017 members, 674 young parents and 343 children, had registered for the shibir. The theme of the National Family Shibir was 'Aap Rijo em Raaji' and for the Children's Shibir, 'Mare Swamine Raji Karva Chhe'. The shibir agenda had been interlaced with speeches, bhajans, slide shows, Swamishri's blessings and darshan, sports and quizzes. The family shibir and children's shibir programs included: Swamishri Cares (slide show), When I needed you, You were there (incidents of kishores), Agna (speech), Divinity, Raas (folk dance), Swamishri's narration of incidents, Photo - story narration by Swamishri, Question - answer sessions and sports.

in the evening assembly volunteers of the bal mandal presented a drama 'Blind Despite Seeing' that imparted the message that parents should spare time with their children, should not over protect them and not expect more than their capacities. Finally Swamishri blessed the assembly.

ph: Swamishri addresses the evening assembly on Yuva Din

w: A teachers’ convention of the ‘Rajkot District Primary Organisation’ was held in the mandir precincts. More than 2,500 primary teachers were present in the convention. At 11.40 am Swamishri blessed the convention, “The primary school teachers here have been blessed with the great service of educating children. It is like nurturing little plants. To give knowledge to children from grades one to seven is of foundational importance. You have to teach them well, inspire them with an inclination to learn and keep them away from addictions. The teachers should teach with the sentiments that the students are your children. Formerly in the ashrams of rishis students were taught self-sufficiency – doing things by themselves. Today we find the bonds of love fading between teachers and students. Science has progressed but it has brought with it many corruptive elements.”
